inventory.categoryThresholdsDesc: P75 = 75th percentile of days since last sale. 75% of SKUs in the category sold more recently than this. Threshold is clamped to 90–365 days and defines when stock becomes "dead".

inventory.healthInfo2: Thresholds adapt per category — we look at the typical selling pace (75th percentile of days since last sale). Fast-moving categories get shorter deadlines, slow-moving ones get longer.
inventory.healthInfo3: Thresholds are clamped between 90 and 365 days. Categories with insufficient data use 180 days as default.
inventory.healthInfo4: Last sale within 70% of the category threshold.
inventory.healthInfo5: Last sale between 70%–100% of the threshold — approaching dead stock.
inventory.healthInfo6: No sale beyond the category threshold.
inventory.healthInfo7: No recorded sale since the product first appeared in inventory.
inventory.healthInfo8: Selling, but stock exceeds 90 days of supply at current velocity.

inventory.turnover.info1: DSI (Days Sales of Inventory) — how many days it takes to sell current stock at current revenue pace.
inventory.turnover.info2: Turnover Ratio — how many times stock rotates per year. Higher = better capital efficiency.
inventory.turnover.info3: Optimal stock is calculated based on lead time (14d), safety stock (7d), and buffer (5d) = 26 days of supply.
inventory.turnover.info4: ABC analysis classifies SKUs by 90-day revenue: A = top 80%, B = next 15%, C = bottom 5%.
inventory.turnover.sellThroughDesc: Metrics based on 90-day sales velocity. Days of Supply shows how long current stock lasts at this pace. STR (Sell-through Rate) = sold / (sold + available) × 100%.

retention.actionDesc: Consider launching a win-back email campaign with special offers for inactive customers.
retention.atRiskExplain: Identifies customers who haven't purchased in 90+ days, grouped by their acquisition cohort. Focus on high-value at-risk customers for win-back campaigns.
retention.insightDecayHalfLife: Retention halves by M{{month}} — focus re-engagement before this point
retention.insightDecayNoHalfLife: Retention stays above half of M1 throughout the period — strong loyalty signal
retention.insightDecayStabilizes: Retention stabilizes at M{{month}} ({{rate}}%) — these are your loyal core
retention.insightFast: {{pct}} of repeat customers return within 30 days - great for consumable products!
retention.insightRevenueImpact: If all cohorts matched the best M1 ({{bestM1}}%), you could gain ~{{amount}}/mo in additional revenue
retention.insightText: Median repurchase time is {{days}} days - consider re-engagement campaigns at 60-day mark.
retention.insightTrendDeclining: M1 retention declined by {{delta}}pp — recent cohorts are less likely to return
retention.insightTrendImproving: M1 retention improved by {{delta}}pp — recent cohorts show stronger repeat behavior
retention.insightTrendStable: M1 retention is stable across cohorts (±1pp)
retention.ltvExplain: Tracks cumulative lifetime value per customer for each cohort over time. Compare cohorts to identify which acquisition periods brought valuable customers.
retention.ltvHowToRead: Each line shows how cumulative LTV (lifetime value per customer) grows over time for a specific cohort. Steeper lines = faster value accumulation. Compare cohorts to identify which acquisition periods brought the most valuable customers.
retention.retentionExplain: Each row is a cohort of customers who made their first purchase in that month. The percentages show what % returned to purchase again in subsequent months.
retention.revenueExplain: Shows revenue retention: what % of original cohort revenue is generated in each subsequent month. Useful for understanding revenue sustainability.
retention.timingExplain: Analyzes how long it takes customers to make their second purchase. Helps optimize re-engagement timing and email automation triggers.
retention.timingTrack: Track when customers typically repurchase to optimize your email automation timing.
retention.tipDesc: Focus on cohorts with high at-risk percentages but also high historical revenue - these customers have demonstrated purchase potential and may respond well to re-engagement.
retention.title: Cohort Analysis
sms.armsShareFilters: One audience, cut into arms in order: the first rule a customer matches wins, and whoever matches none drops out. The filters above apply to all of them equally.
sms.audienceEmpty: Nobody matches these filters. The breakdown below says which rule emptied the list.
sms.basisHint: Sets the tier cut-offs and what “lifetime value” means in the filters above.
sms.buttonNeedsBoth: A button needs both a label and a link, or the gateway will refuse it.
sms.campaignRequired: A campaign name is required to record the roster. Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
sms.campaignsDesc: Rosters frozen at export. Mark a campaign sent once the file has gone to the provider — results are measured from that date.
sms.deliveredOnlyHint: drops the recipients the gateway refused outright, leaving the control intact. Recipients still awaiting a receipt stay in — the provider does not report back to us, so a missing receipt is not a failed delivery. An optimistic bound rather than a clean comparison.
sms.detailsNoMessage: Not recorded — this campaign went out before the text was stored.

sms.exBrand: NEOGEN — ever bought anything of that brand.
sms.exCategory: A parent category takes everything under it.
sms.exCity: Kyiv, Lviv — comma separated, case does not matter.
sms.exFirstOrder: From 01.01.2026 — everyone who came to us this year.
sms.exLtv: From 5 000 ₴ — spent that much in total, on the basis chosen below.
sms.exOrders: From 2 — repeat buyers. 1 to 1 — bought exactly once.
sms.exPromocode: KS-AUG — used exactly this code at least once.
sms.exSource: Where their orders came from. Nothing picked means any.
sms.exportAllTiers: Nothing picked — the file takes every tier, {{total}} contacts.
sms.exportDesc: A campaign name is what lets the roster be frozen — without it the campaign never reaches step 2 and there is nothing to measure.
sms.exportPickedTiers: The file takes {{total}} contacts from the picked tiers.
sms.filterBoughtWithinHint: 180 — bought the above within the last half year, not ever.
sms.filterGroupHowMuchHint: Counted over their whole history, not over the filtered part of it.
sms.filterGroupWhatHint: Did they ever buy this. Several rules here mean all of them at once.
sms.filterGroupWhenHint: The base window is applied first, before every other rule.
sms.filterGroupWhoHint: From the customer card, not from the orders.
sms.filterLastOrderAsDays: Same thing in days: {{from}} to {{to}}. A saved audience keeps the days, which stay true next month; the dates do not.
sms.filterLastOrderHint: 01.01.2026 — 28.05.2026: bought this year, quiet since May.
sms.filterRecencyHint: The same window, counted back from today. 90 is three months of silence.
sms.filterWindowHint: Older than this and the customer is not considered at all. 270 by default, 730 max.
sms.filtersHint: Every rule you add narrows the audience. Leave a field empty and it asks nothing.
sms.forestDesc: Every tier on one scale. The dot is the measured lift, the bar is the interval the true value sits in. A bar that does not touch zero means the effect is shown.
sms.forestDetail: messaged {{target}}% against {{control}}% in the control, interval {{lo}} to {{hi}} pp, p={{p}}, {{contacts}} recipients
sms.forestHint: Hover a row for the figures
sms.forestKeyProven: interval clear of zero — effect shown
sms.freezeHint: tick this on the file you actually send. The list changes daily, so a roster not recorded now can never be reconstructed — and without it the campaign cannot be measured.
sms.funnelNote: The right column is how many that rule removed. Numbers shared across customer records collapse into one — the SMS goes out once.
sms.groupingHint.rfm: Three arms, each with its own control. Answers who responds better — at the price below.
sms.groupingHint.single: Everyone the filters kept, measured together. The sharpest measurement an audience of this size can give.
sms.guideChangingBody: While purchases are few, a per-contact difference multiplied by thousands of recipients swings the totals wildly, negative included. That is noise, not a loss. Read it after 7–14 days, and always next to the p-value.
sms.guideControlBody: When the roster is frozen, each customer lands in the control or in the send by a hash of (customer ID, campaign name). The hash gives a number 0–99, and anything below the chosen percentage goes to the control. The draw runs inside each tier separately, so the control share is the same in VIP, Core and Reactivation. The point of a hash rather than a coin toss is that it repeats: re-exporting the same campaign gives the same split, while a new campaign name reshuffles it — so the same people are not withheld from every campaign in a row. The control is never messaged, including on a repeat send.
sms.guideControlTerm: How the control group is drawn
sms.guideDiffBody: The campaign's result is the gap between the messaged group and the control. The messaged group's own purchase rate means nothing alone: they would have bought anyway.
sms.guideDiffTerm: Everything here is a difference, not a total
sms.guideLiftBody: How many percentage points higher the purchase rate is than the control's. +1.0 pp means one extra buyer per 100 recipients.
sms.guideMarginBody: The same, less the cost of goods. This is the figure that says whether the campaign paid for itself. A product with no cost on file drops out of margin but stays in revenue, so margin reads low.
sms.guidePValueBody: The chance of seeing a gap this size if the campaign does nothing at all. Below 0.05 the effect counts as shown. Above it, there is not enough data yet — which is not the same as there being no effect.
sms.guideRevenueBody: Average revenue per recipient minus average revenue per control member, times the number of recipients. What the campaign brought in beyond ordinary trading.
sms.guideVerdictBody: A campaign is judged only once the messaged group and the control each have at least 5 purchases inside the window. Below that the interval is driven by the correction rather than by anything observed: with 0 purchases in a control of 162 the true rate could still be almost 2%, and on the first real campaign that was the entire measured lift.
sms.guideWindowBody: Purchases count from the moment of sending, for the chosen number of days. Match the window to how long the offer lives: a two-day sale wants 2. Days after it expires add ordinary trading to both arms equally — no effect, more variance — so the result gets harder to see, not easier.
sms.headlineApparent: The campaign appears to have brought in {{revenue}} above the control group.
sms.headlineProven: The campaign brought in {{revenue}} above the control group.
sms.headlineWhyEarly: Not provable yet: {{n}} people in the control group bought, and a verdict needs at least {{min}}. The figure above is an estimate, and its range includes a loss.
sms.headlineWhyProven: The effect is proven: the difference is not explained by chance.
sms.headlineWhyWide: The difference is still indistinguishable from chance: both arms have bought enough, but the spread is wider than the effect.
sms.holdoutExplain: A slice of the audience is deliberately never messaged. It is the only thing the result is measured against — precision comes from withholding more, not from sending more.
sms.holdoutHint: Precision is bought by withholding, not by sending: doubling the control narrows the interval far more than doubling the send. At 10% a single tier cannot show anything short of a 6–12 pp effect. Now: {{target}} messaged, {{holdout}} withheld.
sms.how1: Step 1 — build the audience with filters and freeze the roster.
sms.how2: Step 2 — send the campaign (or mark it sent if it went out by hand).
sms.how3: Step 3 — read the lift against the control group.
sms.howControl: Part of the audience deliberately gets no SMS — that is the control, 10% by default. Without it there is no telling the campaign's effect from purchases that would have happened anyway.
sms.levelAllHint: Nothing picked — every level, including customers who fit none.
sms.markSentFailed: Could not mark the campaign as sent
sms.mdeGood: Comfortable: the last campaign moved conversion by about 2 pp, and this would see it.
sms.mdeHopeless: This will send and prove nothing: no realistic offer moves conversion that far. Raise the control share, or measure with one arm.
sms.mdeLabel: What this campaign will be able to prove
sms.mdeTight: Tight: the last campaign moved conversion by about 2 pp, so a weaker offer would come back unproven.
sms.measureSplitHint: Answers which levels respond better, at the cost of a blunter measurement of each — every level gets its own control group.
sms.messagePlaceholder: Text as the customer will see it
sms.noCampaignsHint: Tick “Record this roster” when you export the file you intend to send.
sms.noControlInTier: No control group in this tier — nothing to compare against.
sms.noRosterData: No roster data for this campaign
sms.noSentCampaigns: No campaign has been sent yet
sms.noSentCampaignsHint: Record a roster at export, then mark it sent. Results appear here afterwards.
sms.notSentWarning: The gateway never took {{n}} of the target arm — they were never messaged. They are left out of the figures so the lift is not understated.
sms.notSentYet: This campaign has no send date yet — mark it sent to measure it.
sms.presetsHint: Save this set of filters to send to the same people again later.
sms.promoReminder: This campaign carries code {{code}} — include it in the text.
sms.rangeInverted: The “{{fields}}” range runs backwards — the first box must not exceed the second. Nothing is being counted until it does.
sms.resultsDesc: The messaged group against its control. The difference is the result — the messaged group's own rate is not.
sms.rosterFrozen: The roster is recorded. Sending is the last irreversible step.
sms.rosterWillFreeze: Creating the campaign records who is in it — target and control alike. The eligible list shifts daily, so this is the only roster the results will have.
sms.ruleHoldoutNote: Who lands in the control is a hash of customer ID and campaign name: re-exporting the same campaign keeps the same split, a new name reshuffles it.
sms.ruleOrderNote: Tiers are tested top to bottom and each customer lands in exactly one — the first that fits. Value is retail only, excluding returns and retired sources.
sms.ruleSingleGroup: Everyone the filters kept, last order within {{days}} days
sms.segmentsDesc: Customers scored on recency, repeat purchases and value. VIP buys anyway — send early access, not a discount.
sms.sendFailed: The gateway refused the send — nothing was marked as sent
sms.sendIrreversible: Sending cannot be undone. The roster is stamped sent and a second send is refused, so the measurement stays honest.
sms.sendPartial: Partly sent: {{unsent}} recipients were not messaged. The campaign is stamped sent — it cannot be retried without messaging the others twice.
sms.sendRecipients: {{target}} will be messaged. {{holdout}} are held back as the control group and will not receive anything.
sms.smsFallbackPreview: What arrives by SMS if Viber cannot deliver:
sms.splitHint: An arm is compared against its own control group. More arms means a sharper picture of who responds — and a blunter measurement of each.
sms.summaryCostFrom: from {{cost}} — one part each, until there is a text
sms.summaryNoPrice: price appears once there is an audience
sms.testAccepted: The gateway accepted the message. ID: {{id}}
sms.testDesc: Check the text before a campaign. Nothing is recorded: no campaign, no roster, no opt-outs.
sms.testNoLinks: An SMS cannot hide a link behind text — paste the full address; the customer sees it as is.
sms.testNotAccepted: The gateway did not accept it: code {{code}}, {{status}}
sms.testPhoneInvalid: Needs a full Ukrainian number: 380 followed by 9 digits.
sms.testStoplisted: Number is on the provider's stoplist
sms.tierRulesHint: The cascade runs top down; whoever matches none of the three is dropped from the audience. Blank uses the standing thresholds.

sms.totals: {{total}} contacts total — {{target}} to send, {{holdout}} held back as control

sms.viberUnavailable: Viber is unavailable: no Viber sender name configured (TURBOSMS_VIBER_SENDER). It is registered separately from the SMS alpha name.
sms.windowConflict: The base window is {{window}} days, so asking for people quiet for {{min}}+ days leaves nobody. Widen the window.
